classification.difficultyReason: Locate each fraction by counting segments on the supplied wall, compare their endpoints across rows, and select the relational symbol. Close pairs such as seven tenths and five sevenths require careful visual comparison, but no new method or inference.

content.prompt: Use the fraction wall to compare these fractions using relational symbols $<$, $>$, and $=$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 2, fraction wall above parts i–xii
spec.description: Nine aligned horizontal rows labelled halves through tenths. Each row has the same whole length and equal subdivisions. Only its leftmost unit fraction is coloured.
spec.mathematics: Row n partitions the common whole into n equal cells for n=2 through 10. Comparing accumulated cell lengths compares fractions.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied reference figure; no comparison answers are included.

answer.worked: On the fraction wall, one third ends before two fifths. Hence $\frac{1}{3}<\frac{2}{5}$.
One third and three ninths end at the same point on the fraction wall. Hence $\frac{1}{3}=\frac{3}{9}$.
One third extends beyond three tenths on the fraction wall. Hence $\frac{1}{3}>\frac{3}{10}$.
One quarter and two eighths end at the same point on the fraction wall. Hence $\frac{1}{4}=\frac{2}{8}$.
One quarter extends beyond two ninths on the fraction wall. Hence $\frac{1}{4}>\frac{2}{9}$.
One quarter ends before three tenths on the fraction wall. Hence $\frac{1}{4}<\frac{3}{10}$.
One fifth ends before two ninths on the fraction wall. Hence $\frac{1}{5}<\frac{2}{9}$.
One fifth and two tenths end at the same point on the fraction wall. Hence $\frac{1}{5}=\frac{2}{10}$.
Four sixths and six ninths end at the same point on the fraction wall. Hence $\frac{4}{6}=\frac{6}{9}$.
Eight ninths end before nine tenths on the fraction wall. Hence $\frac{8}{9}<\frac{9}{10}$.
Two thirds end before seven tenths on the fraction wall. Hence $\frac{2}{3}<\frac{7}{10}$.
Seven tenths end before five sevenths on the fraction wall. Hence $\frac{7}{10}<\frac{5}{7}$.
